segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,
to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping
due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing;
or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.

As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), claimed as one atom and never expanded into classes. 'the driver of' names who controls that vehicle, a relational role and no membership, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency). The aggregate's 'not a stand-in' clause excludes a relational role as membership, which is why 'driver' claims nothing of its own.

st.railway_crossing is the 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail': 'crossing at grade any track or tracks' is a crossing on the level. DEF-NRS-484A-200 makes a railroad 'a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails'; the atom's contract is a crossing of a railway with the roadway, which a streetcar track laid along the street is not, so the definition's exclusion is already the contract's. 'When crossing' anchors the crossing to x: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') while x is on the crossing, and st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') after its footprint has left it, until x has completely crossed (s6). rel.occupies is read only as overlap; st.region_geometry's 'not a stand-in for occupancy' is respected, since the distance is read only past the crossing, beside the occupancy that x had before.

'without stopping' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition that applies: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' is drv.motion.stopped, the halt at one observation, which denotes the halt 'whoever or whatever controls the road user' and holds at a momentary halt because it reads the one observation. The definition's exclusions are not the concept's and the rule carries them beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' by prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, another road user's predicted closest approach to x within the conflict horizon coming within the conflict clearance; 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer' by dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given', role police_officer, indication stop) governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). dev.governs' 'not a stand-in for a position' is respected: it is read only as which region the officer's direction controls. 'fail to completely cross the track or tracks' reads the crossing of s2 and the law's own definition (s6): the halt is forbidden while x is on the crossing (rel.occupies) or less than the stated distance past it (st.region_geometry).

'due to insufficient ... Space for the vehicle on the opposite side' states why the halt happens and is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): x halts with another road user directly ahead of it, the one taking the space beyond the crossing. rel.bearing is the 'direction of b from a in a's frame', whose longitudinal component positive places y ahead of x, on the side toward which x crosses; rel.surface_gap, the 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', at most the queue standstill gap says x stands at the back of y as a queued vehicle does, so the space x needed is taken. rel.surface_gap has no 'not a stand-in' clause; rel.bearing is read as a direction, not a distance. The words name no class for what fills the space, so y is any road user other than x.

The law's own definition of 'completely cross': 'the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail'. st.region_geometry gives 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', so once x is past the crossing its body's nearest point to the crossing, the trailing end, is at least the stated literal from the crossing's boundary; 'past' is read as x having occupied the crossing (rel.occupies) and left it without the distance reaching the literal since, so the trailing end lies beyond the crossing on the side x crossed to. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing 'and its nearest rail', the boundary the distance is read to (reading on s3).

assumptions.meaning: The underside of the road user's vehicle touches, or lacks the clearance to pass over, the surface it is travelling across at the observation.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) crossing a railway crossing at grade: there is a railway crossing r (st.railway_crossing) whose region x's footprint overlaps at the observation (rel.occupies), or overlapped at an earlier observation with x's body less than the s6 literal (15 ft) from r (st.region_geometry distance) at every observation since that one: since(distance(x, r) < 15 ft, occupies(x, r)). A vehicle that halts short of a crossing it has not entered is not crossing; one whose body has reached the literal distance past the crossing has completely crossed and is no longer crossing.
obligation: Violated at an observation where, for a railway crossing r selected as in the applicability (bound again in the obligation with the whole selection: the crossing x occupies, or occupied with its body less than the literal from it at every observation since), x is halted (drv.motion.stopped, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance) and the halt is due to an insufficiency the words name: (1) some road user y other than x lies ahead of x (rel.bearing from x to y, longitudinal component positive) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_standstill_gap, or (2) the declared assumption asm.undercarriage_grounded holds; unless the halt is one the stopping definition excludes: some road user z other than x has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), or a dev.human_direction with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). Compliant at every other observation of the crossing: crossing without halting, or halting only once completely across, meets the duty. Where x is halted on the crossing with no road user ahead within the gap and the assumption undeclared, the cause of the halt is unknown and so is the verdict.

narrowings.why: 'the driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'due to insufficient ... Space' states why the halt happens; it is read through the conduct it explains, the halt directly behind a road user standing ahead within the queue standstill gap, not through a cause the trace cannot show.

'the nearest rail' is read as the rail nearest the vehicle's trailing end once it has crossed, the edge of the crossing region on the side it crosses to, so a vehicle whose body is still on a further track has not completely crossed; the distance is read to the crossing region's boundary as the source maps it.

The stopping definition's exclusion 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' is read for the officer only: a device directs a halt at the place it marks (its stop line, or short of the crossing), and a halt on the tracks or less than the stated distance past them is not at such a place, so no device's indication excuses it; 'other traffic' in the definition is read as every other road user of the scene.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x, a car, enters a level crossing; a truck y stands queued just beyond it. x halts behind y with its body still on the tracks, the gap to y within the standstill gap; no officer directs traffic and no road user moves toward x.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x, alone in the scene, drives over a level crossing at a steady speed and continues well past it without halting.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x drives on a road with no railway crossing and halts behind a queued vehicle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x halts on the crossing with a vehicle y ahead of it; the source declares rel.surface_gap absent and the trace declares no undercarriage assumption, so whether x halts at the back of a queue is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x crosses without halting and halts behind queued y only once its body is farther than the stated distance past the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x halts on the crossing with no road user ahead of it; the trace declares asm.undercarriage_grounded for x at that observation.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a police officer at the crossing directs x to stop (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop, governing the lane x occupies) when it halts.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
param_proposals.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it.
param_proposals.source: Car-following models' standstill (jam) distance, e.g. the Intelligent Driver Model and Wiedemann

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about the sum of two passenger-car half-lengths.
param_proposals.source: Design passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO Green Book design vehicle)

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character at:
A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: 'to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: drv.motion.moving, 'a road user is in motion at the observation ... whoever or whatever controls the road user'; a vehicle at rest has no rate of speed the standard could find unreasonable. 'any person' names who controls the vehicle, a role read through the vehicle's conduct (observable_reading, agency).

'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), one atom, never expanded; 'of any kind or character' adds no class beyond the definition's.

operationalizations.standard: A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: Stopping-sight-distance model (AASHTO Green Book): a speed is reasonable only where the vehicle can halt, after a perception-reaction time and at the deceleration the surface sustains, within the distance it can see along the road (st.sight_distance) and through the air (env.visibility); the surface selects that deceleration (ice or snow, else a wet road or falling precipitation, else dry). Traffic: time-headway convention, the speed times the minimum time headway within the gap to each road user of the traffic ahead in the lane. Other highway conditions: the lateral acceleration in a bend (speed squared times st.curvature) within the acceleration the surface sustains. Width: time-to-line-crossing convention, the speed times the lateral margin needed per unit of speed within the free lateral margin, half of the lane width less the vehicle width. Each measured magnitude enters its bound, so the bound moves with the speed, the gap, the distances, the curvature and the width; the surface condition selects among bounds.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is being driven: x is in motion (drv.motion.moving, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance).
obligation: Surrogate. At the observation x's speed (kin.speed) meets every bound the factors set. Let a be the surface's deceleration: p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.surface_friction_accel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.surface_friction_accel_dry; the stopping distance SD is drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, a), written as a Term.cond over the three calls, each with its own constant parameter. (1) SD is at most the sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance) and at most the visibility distance (env.visibility). (2) For every road user y other than x that is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), x's speed times p.following_min_time_headway is at most the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap). (3) x's speed squared times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most a, selected as above. (4) For every lane l (st.lane) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), x's speed times p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed is at most half of the difference between the lane's width (st.lane_width) and x's width (kin.extent, width). Violated where any bound fails.

narrowings.why: 'any person to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

'the traffic' (DEF-NRS-484A-285: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel') is read only through the road users ahead of x in its own lane, every one of which is using the way for travel, by the time headway to each; oncoming, crossing and adjacent-lane traffic, and traffic on a way with no mapped lane, set no bound.
'surface' is read through env.wet_road and env.ice_or_snow, which select the deceleration; surface texture, loose material and damage carry no atom and are not read.

'width of the highway' is read through the width of the lane x occupies (st.lane_width), the strip its travel uses, not the whole width between the highway's boundary lines; where x occupies no mapped lane the width sets no bound.
'the weather' is read through env.visibility, by its degree, and env.precipitation, which selects the wet deceleration; wind and temperature are not read.
The catch-all 'other highway conditions' is read only through st.sight_distance and st.curvature; grade, works and other conditions are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x, alone in the scene, drives on a dry road in dense fog at a speed whose stopping distance far exceeds the visibility distance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x, alone in the scene, drives at a moderate speed on a dry, straight road with wide lanes in clear weather and a long sight distance; its stopping distance lies within the sight and visibility distances and the lane-keeping margin holds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x stands halted throughout the trace.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares kin.speed absent: whether x moves, and how fast, is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Clear, dry, straight road; x follows y, a car in the same lane, at a gap shorter than its speed times the minimum time headway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x drives through a bend on an icy road at a speed whose lateral acceleration exceeds the ice deceleration, though it would lie within the dry one.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The same bend and speed as branch_2 on a dry road in clear weather, every other bound met.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: A wide vehicle x travels in a narrow lane at a speed whose required lateral margin exceeds half of the lane width less its width; every other bound is met.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.perception_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from sighting a need to halt to applying the brakes, chosen to cover most drivers.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (Green Book), stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_dry
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers achieve and most paved surfaces sustain when dry; also read as the acceleration a dry surface sustains in a bend.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance deceleration rate

param_proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_wet
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration a wet paved surface sustains: a wet-pavement friction coefficient of about a quarter at highway speeds, times gravity; also the acceleration it sustains in a bend.
param_proposals.source: Pavement skid-resistance data (AASHTO Guide for Pavement Friction)

param_proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration an icy or snow-covered surface sustains: a friction coefficient of about a tenth, times gravity; also the acceleration it sustains in a bend.
param_proposals.source: Winter road friction measurements (PIARC Snow and Ice Databook)

param_proposals.name: p.following_min_time_headway
param_proposals.convention: Car-following: the smallest time gap to the road user ahead at which a following driver can still react to its braking; gaps below it are classed as close following.
param_proposals.source: Time-headway criteria of naturalistic driving and traffic-flow studies

param_proposals.name: p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-line-crossing convention: drifting at a heading error of about one degree, a vehicle keeps at least one second before its body reaches the lane edge, so the free lateral margin it needs is its speed times the sine of that error times that time.

contract: The distance a road user would travel from the observation to a halt if it kept its current speed for a reaction time and then slowed at a constant deceleration: its speed at the observation (kin.speed) times `reaction_time`, plus the square of that speed divided by twice `decel`, in metres along its path. It is a quantity of the road user's own motion at the one observation, whoever or whatever controls it, and is zero for a road user standing still. Not denoted: the distance an actual later halt takes; the grade or the surface, which the caller states through the deceleration it passes.

params.name: reaction_time
params.meaning: the time the road user keeps its speed before it begins to slow

params.name: decel
params.meaning: the constant rate at which it slows once it begins to; strictly positive

elements.justification: kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; the distance to a halt depends on that magnitude alone, so neither the direction of motion nor the heading is read.

literals.why: The kinematic factor of constant deceleration: the distance to halt from a speed is the square of the speed over twice the deceleration.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A road user moves at a steady speed; the instance's bounds bracket its speed times the reaction time plus the square of its speed over twice the deceleration, read at that observation.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The same road user; the instance's bounds lie wholly below the value the contract computes.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares kin.speed absent; the value is unknown.

segmentation.text: An operator of a bicycle,
an electric bicycle
or an electric scooter
upon a roadway
shall give all signals by hand and arm
in the manner required by NRS 484B.420 [DEF-NRS-484B-420],
except that the operator may give a signal for a right turn by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.

elements.justification: 'bicycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride ... except a moped'), one atom. 'An operator of' is the rider, a role read through the machine's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

'electric bicycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts'), one atom, never expanded.

'electric scooter' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on in an upright or seated position'), one atom, never expanded.

DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder' is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; its 'not a stand-in for the sidewalk' clause is the definition's own exclusion. 'upon' anchors it to x by rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; a one-way roadway refines st.roadway and is included.

'give all signals by hand and arm': sig.hand_signal is 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}', the signal given by hand and arm; sig.turn_indicator is 'the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}', the signal given otherwise. Every turn signal the rider gives by lamp is to be a signal by hand and arm of the same meaning. The manner borrowed from DEF-NRS-484B-420 ('extended horizontally') is the posture whose meaning the source reads into sig.hand_signal. sig.turn_indicator's 'not a stand-in for the turn itself' is respected: the lamp is read as a signal, never as the turn.

The exception permits a second posture for one meaning: a right-turn signal given 'by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side'. sig.hand_signal carries the meaning of the arm signal given, right, whichever arm and posture give it, so the right-arm signal and the posture the borrowed manner states both read as meaning right and both meet the duty.

applicability: x is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, or DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter) whose footprint overlaps a roadway r (rel.occupies, st.roadway) at the observation.
obligation: At the observation, every turn signal x gives is given by hand and arm: where x's turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator) shows left, x's arm signal (sig.hand_signal) has meaning left, and where it shows right, x's arm signal has meaning right. An arm signal of meaning right meets the duty whichever arm gives it (the exception). An arm signal given with no lamp, and no signal at all, are compliant: this rule judges how signals are given, not whether one is owed.

narrowings.why: 'An operator of' is read through the controlled motion of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, whoever or whatever controls it.

'all signals' is read as the turn signals the rider gives by lamp (sig.turn_indicator): a brake lamp lights as an actuation of the brake, which its contract separates from a signal the rider gives, so it is not read; the posture of the arm beyond the meaning the source reads from it is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x, an electric scooter, rides on a roadway with its right turn indicator flashing and no arm signal (sig.hand_signal no_signal).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x, a bicycle, rides alone on a roadway and signals a left turn by arm (sig.hand_signal left); it has no turn indicator lit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x, a bicycle, rides on a sidewalk with its turn indicator lit and no arm signal; it never occupies a roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x, an electric bicycle on a roadway, shows its left turn indicator; the source declares sig.hand_signal absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x, an electric bicycle on a roadway, shows its right turn indicator and extends its right arm horizontally to the right, which the source reads as sig.hand_signal right.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x, a bicycle on a roadway, gives no signal of any kind and has no indicator lit.

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
upon a highway of this State,
subject to exceptions with respect to parked vehicles as stated in chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS,
must display lighted lamps and illuminating devices as respectively required in this chapter for different classes of vehicles:
(a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise;
(b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead;
and (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less devices moved by human power, electric bicycles and electric scooters), one atom, never expanded.

DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority' is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; its 'not a stand-in for the roadway' clause is respected, since the words name the whole highway. 'upon' anchors it to x by rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. 'of this State' is the reading's jurisdiction: every map this corpus is read against is declared in this State.

'parked vehicles' is read through the conduct parking shows (observable_reading, purpose): a vehicle at a complete halt (drv.motion.stopped, 'a road user is at a complete halt at the observation') whose engine does not run (kin.engine_running, 'the vehicle's engine or motor is running', false). kin.engine_running's 'not a stand-in for motion or a halt' is respected: the halt is read by the concept, the engine by the atom, together. The exceptions themselves are 'stated in chapters 484A to 484E', in no section this line names, so no rule can be composed: the words make parked vehicles subject to their own provisions, and this rule judges the vehicles that are not parked.

'display lighted lamps and illuminating devices': sig.headlamp, 'headlamp state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}', lit at low_beam or high_beam; sig.position_lamp, 'position, parking, cowl or tail lamps lit (the lamps a vehicle shows without its headlamps)'. 'as respectively required in this chapter for different classes of vehicles' points to the chapter's equipment provisions without naming one; the rule reads the lamps every class of the aggregate shows ahead and behind (reading on f4).

env.darkness is 'insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter': the window 'from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise' is that atom with its boundary at the law's literal, which the reading sets the atom's boundary to. The atom has no 'not a stand-in' clause.

env.visibility is the 'visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)': 'unfavorable atmospheric conditions' under which 'persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead' is that distance below the literal. 'persons and vehicles' name what the visibility is of, not road users the rule reads, so no class is claimed. The words' test is the outcome, discernibility at the stated distance, whichever of the two causes they name produces it; the visibility distance is that outcome as the source measures it.

Nearest atoms, with a gap: dev.regulatory_sign is 'a point regulation by catalogue code' and dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', anchored to x by rel.occupies on a travel region (st.travel_region); no code of the catalogue (nor any kind of dev.zone_sign) is a direction to display lighted lamps, so the direction the words name is not carried. DEF-NRS-484A-145's 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority' is read by the device's presence (status).

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint overlaps a highway h (rel.occupies, st.highway); at the observation one of the listed times holds: (a) env.darkness, its boundary set at the f5 literal one-half hour after sunset and before sunrise; or (b) env.visibility below the f6 literal (1,000 ft); or (c) a device governing (dev.governs) a travel region x occupies directs lamps to be displayed (gap: nearest dev.regulatory_sign); and x is not parked under the exception of f3: not (x is halted, drv.motion.stopped with p.motion_speed_tolerance, and its engine does not run, kin.engine_running false).
obligation: x displays lighted lamps: its headlamps are lit (sig.headlamp state low_beam or high_beam) and its position lamps are lit (sig.position_lamp).

narrowings.why: 'parked vehicles' is read through the conduct parking shows: a vehicle halted with its engine not running.
'as respectively required in this chapter for different classes of vehicles' is read as the headlamps and the position lamps lit; the chapter's per-class lists of further lamps are not read.
'official traffic control device' is read by the device's presence on the road: the feature is the evidence of its official status.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: At night (env.darkness), x, a car, drives alone on a highway with its headlamps off and its position lamps off.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives on a highway with low beams and position lamps lit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Daytime, clear air with visibility far beyond the stated distance, no device directing lamps; x drives on a highway with its lamps off.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares env.darkness absent; the air is clear, no device directs lamps, and x drives with its lamps off.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Daytime fog: visibility below the stated distance; x drives with its headlamps off.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: At night, x stands halted beside the roadway with its engine off and its lamps off: it is parked.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard

gaps.proposal: `dev.lamp_use_sign` | a sign directing road users on the stretch it governs (`dev.governs`) to display lighted lamps (headlamps on), with the same structured **conditions** attribute as `dev.zone_sign` | general — decides when lamps are required by a device's direction although neither darkness nor visibility requires them; no code of `dev.regulatory_sign` and no kind of `dev.zone_sign` is such a direction

segmentation.text: Whenever a motor vehicle is being operated
on the traveled portion of the highway, or shoulder adjacent thereto,
during the times specified in NRS 484D.100 [NRS-484D-100-1],
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam,
directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle,
subject to the following requirements and limitations:
Whenever a driver of a vehicle
approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet,
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver.
The lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, specified in subsection 2 of NRS 484D.210
shall be deemed to avoid glare at all times, regardless of road contour and loading.

elements.justification: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), one atom. 'is being operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled conduct (observable_reading, agency): it is in motion (drv.motion.moving, 'a road user is in motion at the observation') or its engine runs (kin.engine_running, 'propulsion is available'), so a vehicle halted in traffic with its engine running is operated and one parked with its engine off is not; kin.engine_running's 'not a stand-in for motion' is respected, motion being read by the concept.

'the traveled portion of the highway' is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', and 'shoulder adjacent thereto' is st.shoulder, 'the part of the highway beside the roadway'; DEF-NRS-484A-095's highway is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', and st.on_way ('the public way a structure region lies on') ties the roadway or shoulder to it. 'on' anchors the region to x by rel.occupies. st.roadway's 'not a stand-in for the sidewalk' and st.highway's 'not a stand-in for the roadway' are respected: the sidewalk is neither region read, and the highway is read only as the way the region lies on.

'use a distribution of light, or composite beam' is the headlamp beam in use: sig.headlamp, 'headlamp state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}'; off is no distribution of light. 'the driver' names who controls the vehicle, read through its conduct (agency).

operationalizations.standard: directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle
operationalizations.convention: Overdriving-the-headlamps convention: a beam reveals what lies ahead at a safe distance where its seeing distance is at least the distance the vehicle needs to halt, the stopping distance of the AASHTO stopping-sight-distance model (perception-reaction time, design deceleration); the low beam's seeing distance is the driver-handbook figure, and the high beam, the uppermost and most intense distribution a vehicle has, is read as revealing the farthest any beam can. The stopping distance moves with the vehicle's speed, so the bound reads the degree of the danger ahead.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) being operated (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance, or kin.engine_running) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway (st.roadway) or a shoulder (st.shoulder) that lies on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway); NRS_484D_100_1 applies to x (ruleApplies, x ↦ x), which gives the times of NRS 484D.100; and NRS_484D_215_1_o2 does not apply to x (ruleApplies, x ↦ x): the limitation that follows governs while x approaches an oncoming vehicle within its distance.
obligation: x's headlamps are lit (sig.headlamp not off), and where the beam in use is the low beam, x's stopping distance (drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, p.surface_friction_accel_dry)) is at most p.low_beam_seeing_distance: the beam in use reveals what lies ahead at the distance x needs to halt, or is the high beam. Violated where the headlamps are off, or the low beam is in use at a speed whose stopping distance exceeds its seeing distance.

narrowings.why: 'is being operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled conduct, in motion or with its engine running, whoever or whatever controls it.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's conduct, the beam it shows.

'directed high enough and of sufficient intensity' is read through the beam in use, each beam with one seeing distance; the aim and intensity of a particular lamp are not observed, and the high beam is read as meeting the standard at any speed, the speed itself being another rule's. 'safe distance' is read as the stopping distance on a dry surface: the words name no surface or weather factor.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives alone on a roadway of a highway on its low beam at a speed whose stopping distance exceeds the low beam's seeing distance; no vehicle comes toward it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives alone on a roadway of a highway on its high beam; no other road user is present.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Daytime, clear air, no device directing lamps: NRS_484D_100_1 does not apply, and x drives with its lamps off.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives on a roadway; the source declares sig.headlamp absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives fast on its low beam while a car comes toward it within the stated distance, headings opposed: NRS_484D_215_1_o2 applies throughout the trace, so this duty does not.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives slowly on its low beam: its stopping distance lies within the low beam's seeing distance.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives on the shoulder of a highway with its headlamps off.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.perception_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from sighting a need to halt to applying the brakes, chosen to cover most drivers.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (Green Book), stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.surface_friction_accel_dry
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers achieve and most paved surfaces sustain when dry; also read as the acceleration a dry surface sustains in a bend.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance deceleration rate

param_proposals.name: p.low_beam_seeing_distance
param_proposals.convention: Seeing distance of a low beam: the distance ahead within which a low beam reveals persons and vehicles, about 160 ft.
param_proposals.source: Driver handbooks (e.g. the Nevada DMV Driver Handbook) and IIHS headlight evaluations

segmentation.text: Whenever a motor vehicle is being operated
on the traveled portion of the highway, or shoulder adjacent thereto,
during the times specified in NRS 484D.100 [NRS-484D-100-1],
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam,
directed high enough and of sufficient intensity to reveal persons and vehicles at a safe distance in advance of the vehicle,
subject to the following requirements and limitations:
Whenever a driver of a vehicle
approaches an oncoming vehicle within 500 feet,
the driver shall use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver.
The lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam, specified in subsection 2 of NRS 484D.210
shall be deemed to avoid glare at all times, regardless of road contour and loading.

elements.justification: The limitation qualifies the duty of the opening clause, so its frame is that clause's: 'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), one atom; 'is being operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled conduct (agency): in motion (drv.motion.moving) or with its engine running (kin.engine_running, whose 'not a stand-in for motion' is respected, motion being read by the concept).

'the traveled portion of the highway' is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', and 'shoulder adjacent thereto' is st.shoulder, 'the part of the highway beside the roadway'; st.on_way ties either to the highway (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'), and rel.occupies anchors it to x. The sidewalk is no region read, and the highway is read only as the way the region lies on, as the 'not a stand-in' clauses require.

'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), one atom; 'a driver of' is the role of whoever controls it, read through the vehicle's conduct (agency).

'approaches an oncoming vehicle': rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing', with its cosine tolerance; 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed for the other road user. rel.oncoming's 'not a stand-in for the direction a road user approaches an intersection from' does not apply: no intersection approach is read, only two vehicles meeting. 'within 500 feet' is the distance between the two vehicles: rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', at most the literal.

'use a distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver': sig.headlamp, 'headlamp state ∈ {off, low_beam, high_beam}'. The aim is not observed; the law itself deems the lowermost beam to avoid glare (e10, e12), so the duty is met by the low beam; the high beam, directed higher, is read as projecting glare, and off is no distribution of light at all.

'The lowermost distribution of light, or composite beam' borrowed from DEF-NRS-484D-210-1-2 ('lowermost distribution of light') is the low beam, sig.headlamp state low_beam, the lowest of the states the atom lists.

'shall be deemed to avoid glare at all times, regardless of road contour and loading': a beam showing sig.headlamp low_beam meets the duty of e9 wherever x is and however it is loaded, so no grade, curvature or load is read.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) being operated (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance, or kin.engine_running) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway (st.roadway) or a shoulder (st.shoulder) that lies on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway); NRS_484D_100_1 applies to x (ruleApplies, x ↦ x); and some road user y other than x, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), is oncoming to x (rel.oncoming with p.oncoming_cos_tolerance: headings opposed and closing) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most the e8 literal (500 ft).
obligation: x shows its low beam (sig.headlamp state low_beam), the lowermost distribution the law deems to avoid glare. Violated where it shows its high beam, or its headlamps are off.

narrowings.why: 'is being operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled conduct, in motion or with its engine running, whoever or whatever controls it.
'a driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's conduct, whoever or whatever controls it.

'so aimed that the glaring rays are not projected into the eyes of the oncoming driver' is read through the beam in use: the low beam, which the law deems to avoid glare, meets it, and the high beam is read as projecting glare; the aim of a particular lamp is not observed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives on a roadway of a highway on its high beam while y, a car, comes toward it within the stated distance, headings opposed and closing.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same meeting, with x on its low beam.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: At night, x drives alone on a roadway of a highway on its high beam: no vehicle comes toward it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: At night, y comes toward x within the stated distance; the source declares sig.headlamp absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: At night, y comes toward x but stays farther than the stated distance throughout; x keeps its high beam.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: At night, y comes toward x within the stated distance and x drives with its headlamps off.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_cos_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which another vehicle's heading still counts as oncoming: about forty-five degrees, which keeps vehicles meeting on a bend and excludes crossing traffic.
param_proposals.source: Geometric convention for opposing-direction classification (headings within a half right angle of opposed)
